one_liner: Twilio has a broad REST API with free-trial signup (no card) giving working Account SID/Auth Token credentials; Basic auth with API keys is primary, and an official docs-only MCP exists.
auth_notes: Main documented method is HTTP Basic using API key SID/secret or Account SID/Auth Token. OAuth 2.0 apps (client credentials and authorization code) exist but are newer and tied to Twilio accounts, so Basic/API key is safest primary for multi-user. JWT Access Tokens are minted for client SDKs.
access_notes: Free 30-day trial, no credit card, with product-specific free units; same credentials as upgraded accounts. Trial has restrictions (verified numbers only) but is enough to build and test. Upgrade is pay-as-you-go.
blocker_notes: No real blocker; trial accounts have messaging restrictions and expire after 30 days, but upgrading is pay-as-you-go and self-serve.

evidence.quote: Twilio supports three authentication methods. Choose based on your security requirements and integration needs
Twilio supports HTTP Basic authentication. Use your API key as the username and your API key secret as the password.
Access Tokens can be generated by calling the Token API endpoint with the right set of parameters and values.
When you create a Twilio account, you start with a free 30-day trial that lets you explore Twilio products before upgrading.
Your Twilio trial account uses the same account credentials (Account SID and Auth Token) that you use after you upgrade.
